author: yorickdowne
content:
Because it came up in ACDE 244, current status of rolling history expiry for `33_024` epochs. (Maybe this time without being warned)
- Reth, Erigon, Nimbus EL support it
- Nethermind supports it for period of 1 year; next release should allow a shorter period
- Besu broken since `26.2.0`. They know and are working on a fix. Support is experimental behind an `-X` flag
- Ethrex has an active PR, I expect it in a release Soon(tm)
- Geth has a PR that sina opened and lightclient commented on. Maybe lightclient can say whether this can make it into Geth by Glamsterdam

author: yorickdowne
content: I love the idea of amending EIP-4444

author: tersec
content: if nothing else, it's the brand by which it's known and otherwise people will keep looking up 4444 and seeing stale numbers

author: kevaundray
content: Reth doesn't have it 33_024 epochs by default no?

author: yorickdowne
content: Not by default. It's supported. `--prune.bodies.distance 1056768 --prune.receipts.distance 1056768` plus whatever other prune settings. Their default is an archive node

author: yorickdowne
content: DB ends up being around 400 GiB with that

author: yorickdowne
content: My full prune settings for an expired Reth are `--block-interval 5 --prune.senderrecovery.full --prune.accounthistory.distance 10064 --prune.storagehistory.distance 10064 --prune.transactionlookup.distance 10064 --prune.bodies.distance 1056768 --prune.receipts.distance 1056768`

author: kevaundray
content: Thats smaller than I was expecting; tbc the total storage for reth node is 400GB?

author: yorickdowne
content: 400 GiB not GB, and yes that's total. Last tested recently. My records of DB size by clients, keeping in mind these data are outdated rapidly: <https://ethdocker.com/Usage/ResourceUsage#disk-and-ram-requirements>

author: yorickdowne
content: Manufacturers sell storage in GB (power of 10) and an OS counts GiB (2**10 based)

author: yorickdowne
content: I wouldn't use a 1TB drive, particularly with blobs and state growth; but 2TB is completely feasible with rolling history expiry

author: yorickdowne
content: That's roughly 1.8 TiB, plenty of space even for a supernode
